To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution of GR mRNA in the brain is similar to that of GR protein and that GR mRNA is expressed in both neuronal and nonneuronal brain cells.
GR mRNA is expressed in neurons in a wide variety of brain regions and that the relative distribution pattern of the mRNA in these regions is similar to that reported for GR protein.
the glucocorticoid (GC) receptor (GR), a ligand-activated transcription factor, is expressed in a wide variety of brain regions and that GR expression in the brain is developmentally regulated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of mapping the distribution of specific mRNAs in brain tissue.
the development and application of in situ hybridization methods for mapping the distribution of specific messenger RNA in the brain and other tissues.
the development and characterization of a new method for the in situ hybridization analysis of mRNA in the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rat brain is rich in GR mRNA and protein, and the distribution of GR in the brain is consistent with the hypothesis that the receptor is involved in mediating the effects of glucocorticoids on the brain.
the rat GR gene is expressed in the brain in a region-specific manner and that GR protein is expressed in a manner consistent with the expression of its mRNA.
the distribution of GR mRNA in the brain is very similar to the distribution of GR protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GR is expressed in many brain regions, but that the highest concentrations of GR are found in the hippocampus, hypothalamus, olfactory bulb, and thalamus.
glucocorticoid receptors are present in many areas of the brain, including the hippocampus, amygdala, hypothalamus, thalamus, and cortex, as well as the cerebellum.
GR is expressed in many different brain nuclei, with a high degree of regional heterogeneity, and that this expression pattern is similar in the male rat and mouse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative distribution GR protein in different regions of the brain is determined by the relative distribution of the GR mRNA.
the GR mRNA is expressed in the hippocampus and the hypothalamus, which are two regions of the brain that are important for stress regulation and the regulation of the HPA axis.

glucocorticoid receptors are expressed in a variety of brain regions, and the levels of expression in these regions are consistent with a role for glucocorticoids in the regulation of neuronal function.
